headline: Record investment sales lift earnings, buybacks trim shares
summary_short: Primerica's Q2 2026 revenue rose 9% y/y to $865 million and diluted EPS climbed 19% to $6.45, as record investment product sales of $4.4 billion (+23%) offset a 4% decline in Term Life pre-tax income; the company repurchased $135 million of stock and declared a $1.20/share dividend.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue rose 9% y/y to $865.1M (adjusted operating revenue +8.5% to $863.4M). ISP revenue grew 21% to $360.5M on record $4.4B product sales (+23%) and $140B client assets (+16%), lifting ISP pre-tax income 31% to $104.2M. Term Life revenue was roughly flat; pre-tax income fell 4% to $148.5M on higher insurance expenses. Net income rose 13% to $202.3M; diluted EPS +19% to $6.45 (adjusted operating EPS +17% to $6.41), aided by a lower 21.7% tax rate and 5% fewer diluted shares after $135M of buybacks. Cash fell 7% q/q to $600.2M; equity held flat at $2,523M.

drivers.explanation: Company-disclosed: the Investment and Savings Products segment drove growth on strong client demand and favorable equity markets, while Term Life provided stable, predictable earnings; buybacks further lifted per-share results.
Company-disclosed: sales growth was driven by strong client demand and attractive product offerings, while favorable equity market performance contributed to client asset value growth.
Company-disclosed: ISP revenue increased 21% on sales-based commissions in line with commissionable sales and asset-based commissions outpacing asset growth on favorable product mix.
Derived-arithmetic: a 31% increase in ISP segment pre-tax income more than offset a 4% decline in Term Life segment pre-tax income.
Company-disclosed: net income growth reflects higher pre-tax income plus a lower 21.7% effective tax rate versus 23.9% in the prior-year quarter.
Derived-arithmetic: EPS growth of 19% outpaced net income growth of 13% because weighted-average diluted shares fell 5% y/y from share repurchases.
Derived-arithmetic: adjusted operating income growth of 11% combined with the 5% reduction in diluted share count produced 17% adjusted EPS growth.
Company-disclosed: share count fell as the Company repurchased $135 million of common stock during the quarter, part of approximately $352 million returned to stockholders year-to-date.
Company-disclosed: cash declined sequentially as the Company used $135 million for buybacks and approximately $37 million for dividends during the quarter.
Derived-arithmetic: equity was roughly flat as retained-earnings growth from net income was largely offset by buybacks and a wider negative unrealized-securities component of AOCI.
